coordinate_conventions.slope_domain: real numbers excluding vertical-line undefined cases

admissible_constructions: draw line through two distinct points
erect perpendicular from radius to tangent point
translate, rotate, and reflect figures in the plane

rules.name: Two distinct points determine a unique line
rules.operation: Through two distinct points there exists exactly one line.
examples: Points A and B with A != B determine line AB
counterexamples: If A = B, no unique line is determined by the distinct-point rule

rules.name: Segment as bounded part of a line
rules.input_form: points A, B on a line
preconditions: A and B lie on a common line
rules.operation: Define the segment as the bounded part of the line between endpoints A and B inclusive.
examples: If A and B lie on a line, segment AB has finite length
counterexamples: Treating a segment as infinite in both directions is invalid

rules.name: Ray as directed half-line
rules.operation: Define ray AB as starting at A and extending through B indefinitely.
examples: Ray AB and ray BA are different in standard orientation-sensitive notation
counterexamples: Treating ray AB as identical to segment AB is invalid

rules.name: Distance symmetry
rules.operation: Swap endpoints without changing unsigned distance.
examples: AB = BA as lengths
counterexamples: Directed vectors are not the same object as unsigned distance

rules.name: Segment length nonnegativity
rules.operation: Segment lengths are nonnegative and vanish only when endpoints coincide.
examples: If A != B then AB > 0
counterexamples: Assigning a negative segment length is invalid

rules.name: Angle measure additivity
rules.input_form: angle ABC split by interior point D
preconditions: D lies in the interior of angle ABC
rules.operation: Add adjacent interior angle measures to recover the whole angle.
examples: Splitting a 70 degree angle into 20 and 50 degrees preserves total measure
counterexamples: Adding nonadjacent angles without the interior-point condition is invalid

rules.name: Triangle angle sum
rules.operation: Apply the Euclidean triangle angle-sum rule.
examples: If angles are 50 and 60, the third angle is 70
counterexamples: Applying the Euclidean angle-sum rule unchanged in non-Euclidean settings is invalid

rules.name: Exterior angle theorem
rules.output_form: exterior angle equals sum of remote interior angles
rules.operation: Use the exterior-angle relation in a Euclidean triangle.
examples: If remote interior angles are 40 and 55, the exterior angle is 95
counterexamples: Using the adjacent interior angle instead of the remote pair is invalid

rules.name: Triangle inequality
rules.output_form: each side less than the sum of the other two
preconditions: a, b, c are interpreted as side lengths
rules.operation: Check whether three lengths can form a triangle.
examples: 3, 4, 5 satisfy triangle inequality
counterexamples: 1, 2, 4 do not form a triangle

rules.name: SSS congruence
rules.input_form: two triangles with three matching corresponding sides
rules.operation: Infer triangle congruence from equality of all corresponding side lengths.
examples: Matching side triples 3,4,5 and 3,4,5 imply congruence under correspondence
counterexamples: Unmatched correspondence invalidates the claim

rules.name: SAS congruence
rules.input_form: two triangles with two sides and included angle matching
preconditions: The angle is included between the matched sides
rules.operation: Infer congruence from side-angle-side data.
examples: Equal side-angle-side data yields congruence
counterexamples: Using a nonincluded angle does not invoke SAS

rules.name: AA similarity
rules.input_form: two triangles with two equal corresponding angles
rules.operation: Infer triangle similarity from angle-angle data.
examples: Matching angles 40 and 60 imply similarity
counterexamples: Matching only one angle is insufficient

rules.name: Similar triangle side proportions
preconditions: The triangles are already known to be similar
rules.operation: Transfer similarity into proportional side-length relations.
examples: If scale factor is 2, corresponding side lengths double
counterexamples: Corresponding sides need not be equal unless the scale factor is 1

rules.name: Distance formula
rules.operation: Compute Euclidean distance in the Cartesian plane.
examples: Distance between (0,0) and (3,4) is 5
counterexamples: Adding raw coordinate differences without squaring is invalid

rules.name: Midpoint formula
rules.operation: Compute the midpoint of a segment in the Cartesian plane.
examples: Midpoint of (0,0) and (4,2) is (2,1)
counterexamples: Dividing only one coordinate sum by 2 is invalid

rules.name: Slope formula
rules.operation: Compute slope between two points with distinct x-coordinates.
examples: Slope through (1,2) and (3,6) is 2
counterexamples: Vertical lines do not have finite slope in the ordinary real-number sense

rules.name: Invalid triangle equality heuristic
rules.input_form: two matching sides in two triangles
rules.operation: Mark the inference from two side matches alone to full congruence as invalid in general.
counterexamples: Two sides alone do not determine a unique triangle in general

rules.name: Invalid coordinate distance shortcut
rules.operation: Mark Manhattan-distance substitution for Euclidean distance as invalid in this geometry setting.
counterexamples: Between (0,0) and (3,4), Euclidean distance is 5, not 7

rules.name: Radius-tangent perpendicularity
rules.input_form: circle center O, tangent point P
rules.output_form: OP perpendicular to tangent line at P
preconditions: The line is tangent to the circle at P
rules.operation: Use the radius-to-tangent perpendicularity fact at the point of tangency.
examples: If line l is tangent to circle O at P, then OP is perpendicular to l
counterexamples: A secant line through P is not justified as tangent by this rule alone

rules.name: Inscribed angle theorem
preconditions: The angle is inscribed in a circle
rules.operation: Relate an inscribed angle to its intercepted arc.
examples: An inscribed angle intercepting an 80 degree arc measures 40 degrees
counterexamples: Assigning the whole arc measure to the inscribed angle is invalid

rules.name: Triangle area formula
preconditions: Base and corresponding height are measured in compatible length units
rules.operation: Compute triangle area as one half times base times height.
examples: Triangle with base 10 and height 4 has area 20
counterexamples: Omitting the factor one half is invalid

rules.name: Circle area formula
rules.operation: Compute circle area from radius.
examples: Radius 3 gives area 9pi
counterexamples: 2pi r is circumference, not area

rules.name: Cylinder volume formula
rules.input_form: cylinder radius r and height h
rules.operation: Compute right circular cylinder volume from base radius and height.
examples: Radius 2 and height 5 give volume 20pi
counterexamples: Using pi r h omits one factor of r and is invalid

rules.name: Rigid motion preserves distance and angle measure
rules.input_form: translation, rotation, or reflection of a figure
preconditions: The transformation is a rigid motion
rules.operation: Use rigid-motion invariance to preserve lengths and angle measures.
examples: A translated triangle is congruent to the original triangle
counterexamples: A dilation with scale factor 2 does not preserve lengths

rules.name: Coordinate proof by slope or distance invariants
preconditions: The required coordinates and nondegeneracy conditions are defined
rules.operation: Use slope equality, negative reciprocal slopes, or equal distances as coordinate proof tools.
examples: Equal slopes show two nonvertical lines are parallel
counterexamples: Claiming perpendicularity from unequal slopes alone is invalid

rules.name: Circle standard form in coordinates
rules.output_form: circle with center (h,k) and radius r
rules.operation: Interpret the standard coordinate form of a circle.
examples: (x-1)^2 + (y+2)^2 = 9 has center (1,-2) and radius 3
counterexamples: A negative value of r^2 does not represent a real circle

rules.name: Parabola standard form
rules.operation: Interpret the vertical standard form of a parabola.
examples: y = 2(x-1)^2 + 3 has vertex (1,3)
counterexamples: Interpreting y = a(x-h)^2 + k as a circle is invalid
